criteria.name: Correct identity and source-backed footprint
evidence: Purdue GIS feature FID 757 identifies Alpha Gamma Delta (SOAGD) at 1010 David Ross Road.
The saved mesh base contains all 30 distinct transformed source-ring vertices; independently recomputed maximum residual is 0.000000000 m.
The housing operator independently lists the Beta Xi property at the same address.
criteria.uncertainty: The campus-map polygon is not a certified survey and its structural-edge convention and positional tolerance are unpublished.

criteria.name: Position, orientation, and scale/dimensions
evidence: The footprint vertices match the Purdue WGS 84 polygon after the documented local-campus transform.
The wall shell preserves source orientation and scale.
criteria.uncertainty: No source records georeference the front door or porch; the selected west-facing side is a builder estimate.

criteria.name: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
evidence: The Meyer Najem project description calls the house two stories, consistent with the modeled two levels.
The GIS NUM_LEVELS field reports 1, so the level-count conflict remains unresolved.
A stylized exact-address illustration supports a pitched roof silhouette, but the model's 7.6 m eaves, 10.0 m ridge, and compact central gable are not dimensioned by a plan.
criteria.uncertainty: No measured elevations or roof plan were found; roof profile and absolute height are estimates.

criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
evidence: The custom illustration depicts a two-story cream house with pitched roof, columned entry, and red double doors.
The model includes repeated windows, a portico, red door, front steps, cream walls, and a central gable.
Visual inspection of preview_detail.png shows the intended elements, though the gable reads as a small central roof block and the facade rhythm is schematic.
criteria.uncertainty: The illustration is stylized rather than a measured photo, and no georeferenced facade reference confirms the door side, proportions, materials, or window rhythm.

criteria.name: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
evidence: Blender reopened massing_house_301841608_d56a4c4.blend with exactly one mesh object in Asset_massing_house_301841608_d56a4c4 and identity transforms.
The asset contains 2098 vertices and 1412 faces, with 0 external unpacked images.
A dedicated builder, raw GIS feature, structured source notes, validation, and preview are present.
criteria.uncertainty: No portability issue was found in the assigned library.

direct_source_checks: Fraternity Housing Corporation page lists Beta Xi at 1010 David Ross Road, year built 1965, capacity 74, and 23,288 square feet.
Meyer Najem page identifies a 5,000-square-foot renovation and calls the project two stories; it does not establish total-building area or elevations.
Two Tulips product page identifies the illustration as the house at 1010 David Ross Road; it is a stylized design reference, not an architectural drawing.

findings: Identity and source footprint are strong; all 30 GIS base vertices match at project-transform precision.
The two-story model conflicts with the GIS NUM_LEVELS=1 field, whose counting convention is not documented.
The roof and entry vocabulary have an exact-address illustration as a reference, but the gable scale and entrance orientation are not verified.
The facade reads as a basic massing with sparse schematic windows; roof, heights, and entrance details remain uncertain.
